title: Convicted rapist Russell Brand under investigation for claiming innocence from behind bars
summary: The Ministry of Justice in the U.K. is investigating whether comedian and convicted rapist Russell Brand is guilty of breaking prison rules after his wife shared a message from Brand on his YouTube…

image.caption: Comedian and actor Russell Brand, seen here accompanied by his wife Laura Brand at Southwark Crown Court in London earlier this month, is being investigated by British authorities for breaking prison rules about making public statements. (Thomas Krych/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

The Ministry of Justice in the U.K. is investigating whether comedian and convicted rapist Russell Brand is guilty of breaking prison rules after his wife shared a message from Brand on his YouTube channel claiming his innocence.
Brand's wife read his statement to his millions of YouTube subscribers on Sunday

The Ministry of Justice in the U.K. is investigating whether comedian and convicted rapist Russell Brand broke prison rules about public statements after his wife shared a message from Brand on his YouTube channel claiming his innocence.

"I am not guilty for the offences I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening," said his wife Laura Brand, saying she was reading a note from Brand from prison to his 6.6 million subscribers.
In the U.K., prisoners are banned from making statements that could cause distress to victims. Breaking that rule could result in Brand receiving an extended sentence or losing privileges.
Brand, 51, is currently serving a 10-and-a-half-year sentence for rape and sexual assault.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham's spokesperson called the statement "appalling," and said it is being "urgently investigated."
"Prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress ​to victims, and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances," the spokesperson said.
Brand, seen here leaving Southwark Crown Court in London earlier this month, was convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault. (Alastair Grant/The Associated Press)
The spokesperson added that prisoners could not ​get around the rules by asking another person to read their comments.
U.K. Justice Secretary Alex Norris posted about the statement from Brand on X, saying, "I expect action to be taken if he is found to have broken the rules."
Possible sentence increase
The statement came at the 54-minute mark of the couple's weekly podcast episode, part of which was pre-recorded.
"Russell has asked me to read something to you today," said Laura Brand, followed by the claim of innocence from her husband.

If he is found to have broken the rules, Brand could face restrictions on social visits and communication, or lose privileges such as access to time in the gym or TV. It could also result in an extension of his prison sentence.
Laura Brand, seen here arriving at Southwark Crown Court in London earlier this month, shared Brand's statement on the couple's weekly podcast. (Kin Cheung/The Associated Press)

Brand rose to prominence in the 2000s as a comedian, broadcaster and Hollywood star, starring in movies such as Forgetting Sarah Marshall and Get Him to the Greek and working for MTV, BBC and Channel Four. He has since turned to YouTube, where he's made a name for himself as an evangelical influencer and right-wing conspiracy theorist.
Brand was accused by an additional six women of sexual misconduct last week, following his conviction.
He has already been convicted of a rape dating back to 2009, as well as three sexual assaults. He was sentenced to nine years in prison for the rape, and 35 months in prison for the sexual assaults.
Brand has denied the accusations, and claimed he has never had non-consensual sex.
With files from Reuters
